items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: he got a crazy jazz sound out of this drum with the megaphone. And that's when I decided that was for me.

ctx.x: In fact, that's when I first saw a Coca Cola bottle being used as a mute. I think I was about 6 or 7 years old at the time, but I remember it well.

And I saw him playing the drums, and he was singing, which I can't do -- but he was singing, and he also would take the megaphone and put it on the snare drum and would blow through it and he got a crazy jazz sound out of this drum with the megaphone. And that's when I decided that was for me.

Although, like my father, my father had -- he did not want me to be a musician; he was deadly against me being a musician, because my cousin Harold and Lettego and them, all they would do was sit up there and drink all night and sleep all day, and spend all the money they made -- and Daddy just thought that was not the kind of life for me, although I wish he had lived to see what happened and the end result, as far as my being a musician, because I think he would have been pretty proud to have seen what happened…
